record: Canonical hydrograph shape sensitivity (defence brief item A1)

shape.note: Both members measured with the same function that produced the published production-member timescales, so the numbers are commensurable. Hours above a shape fraction is the statistic the progression barrier responds to: a pipe only advances while the instantaneous head exceeds the equilibrium head, which happens close to the crest.

phase1.note: Both arms share one prior sample, so every difference is physical and the bootstrap interval is paired over shared row indices. Gate 1 asserts each baseline against its persisted production sweep; gate 2 asserts the raw static probabilities exactly equal between arms.

surface.note: Overflow and fluvial scour re-executed on the alternate member so the dominance share compares like with like. The committed contract set is asserted unchanged.

peak_shortcut.note: The denominator is the Phase 2 rejection fraction, which the replay computes from the observed 2016 record and not from any canonical member, so it is exactly invariant and Phase 2 was not re-run. The numerator is the prior transient curve read at the observed peak, which is where the shape enters. Exposure is therefore one-sided.

phase3.note: The composition step is imported from the production campaign driver, so the baseline gate exercises the production code path. Nothing under results/system_integration/phase3/ is written.
phase3.surface_scope: both mechanisms re-conditioned on the alternate member, so the dominance share compares like with like

ladder.note: The production ladder is the persisted, gate-verified record; only the alternate arm is computed here. Gate 3 asserts the four static comparators, the two analytic sustained-peak limits and the whole static Shapley lattice bit-identical between the arms, so exactly one telescoping step in each ladder is shape-exposed.
